name: cap-errors-use
description: How to consume failures from this platform: the three members you actually branch on, what a human, an agent and an event each get back, two worked failures, and why adding a new failure type or swapping the component that produces it does not change code you already wrote. Load it when writing a caller, a client or a retry policy against the platform, when handling what comes back from an entry envelope, when deciding what to do with a refusal, or when someone is about to string-match a message to work out what went wrong.

purpose.text: Make the failure half of the platform usable in three members: read type to know what happened, read retryable to know whether to try again, read detail to fix it. Nothing else is required of a caller.
purpose.quote: Typed and machine-readable. Never parsed from prose

operations.name: read (proposed)
operations.input: whatever came back when something failed, from any entry kind
operations.output: the type member, which is a registered URI; branch on it, never on title or detail

operations.name: retry (proposed)
operations.output: the retryable boolean and, where present, retry_after_s; a caller never derives either from the status code

operations.name: explain (proposed)
operations.output: detail for a person, and causes innermost-last when the failure was delegated; neither is ever parsed by a machine

shapes.name: Worked example 1 (proposed): a human submits an entry envelope with no budget

schema.title: Envelope failed schema validation
schema.description: Exit code 2, body on stdout with media type application/problem+json, nothing written to the ledger.

shapes.name: Worked example 2 (proposed): an agent's next step would cross the ceiling

schema.title: A step would cross the budget ceiling
schema.description: Exit code 2, refused before the step ran, so the ledger shows no dispatch for it.

examples.title: A step would cross the budget ceiling
examples.detail: step fix#2 estimated 120000 micros, 41000 remain of a 400000 ceiling

invariants.text: A human, an event, a schedule and an external system or agent get the same object. All four entry kinds enter through the same shape, and the failure half is not specialised per entry, so one handler covers every way work arrived.
invariants.quote: All four enter through the same shape.

invariants.text: Proposed: there is nothing to switch on. A caller does not request typed errors, cannot decline them, and has no error-handling configuration to get wrong; agentic-stack states the no-opt-out rule (F-b1-08) and cap-errors states the shape (F-b4-07).

Enhancing one aspect leaves the rest untouched: adding a registry row, changing a title, or swapping which adapter produces the body changes nothing in a caller that reads type and retryable, because those are the only members it was ever asked to branch on.
invariants.quote: Composability allows enhancing particular aspects of any element without touching the rest.

invariants.text: Three members are the whole obligation on a caller, because a contract that is daunting or overly complex will not be used.
invariants.quote: It cannot be daunting or overly complex, or no one will use it.

invariants.text: Proposed: an unrecognised type is safe to treat as a hard failure with retryable read from the body. cap-errors states that the registry is closed (see its Invariants), so a type a caller has not seen is new, not malformed, and the retry decision is still on the wire.

instructions.action: Branch on the type member and nothing else. Do not match on title, detail, exit codes or log lines.
instructions.why: Errors are typed and machine-readable, never parsed from prose; title and detail are written for people and may be reworded without notice.
instructions.quote: Typed and machine-readable. Never parsed from prose

instructions.action: Read retryable from the body rather than deciding from the status code, and honour retry_after_s when it is present.
instructions.why: The wait for a rate-limited or temporarily unavailable call is knowable at the source and not at the caller: best practice for this standard is to include Retry-After on 429 and 503 responses, and two 503s can differ on whether retrying helps at all.

instructions.action: Show detail to a person and stop there. Do not parse it, log it as the failure identity, or key metrics on it.
instructions.why: The detail field should help developers fix the problem without contacting support, which means it is prose written for a reader and is free to change whenever a clearer sentence is found.
instructions.quote: The detail field should help developers fix the problem without contacting support.

instructions.action: Write one failure handler for all four entry kinds - a human, an event, a schedule, and an external system or agent - instead of one per intake path.
instructions.why: All four enter through the same shape, so a per-entry handler is duplicated work that will drift the moment one path gets a new failure type.
instructions.quote: All four enter through the same shape.

instructions.action: When a failure was delegated, read causes innermost-last to find the origin, and report the outer type as what happened to you.
instructions.why: Proposed. The outer type is the contract the caller was promised; the inner chain is context. Reporting the innermost type outward makes a caller's own interface change whenever a component it never named changes.

instructions.action: Treat an unfamiliar type as a hard failure and use the retryable member, rather than failing closed on the whole response or guessing from the status.
instructions.why: Proposed. New registry rows are added over time; a caller that rejects anything it does not recognise turns every registry addition into a client outage, which is exactly the coupling that composability is meant to remove.

instructions.action: Read the two worked examples above before writing the handler, then read cap-errors only if you need the full member set or the registry, and cap-errors-implement only if you are producing failures rather than consuming them.
instructions.why: Proposed. Three members and two examples are the whole consuming surface; loading the contract and the build guidance to write a caller is the kind of weight that stops a platform from being used.

best_practices.text: Proposed: log the type and the correlation identifier together. cap-errors states why the correlation identifier is on the body; what it buys a caller is that one identifier finds the platform-side record of the same failure without a timestamp search.

Proposed: when a validation failure comes back, fix every field it names before resubmitting. The platform returns all validation errors at once with field-level detail, so a resubmit that fixes one field is a round trip spent learning what you were already told.

Proposed: do not build a retry loop around a refusal. A policy denial and a budget exhaustion are deterministic, arrive before any spend, and carry retryable false; retrying them burns the caller's own budget and changes nothing.

definition_of_done.criterion: `cd examples/end-to-end && bash test.sh`. Section 5 submits an entry envelope with its budget removed and asserts: exit code 2, the answer carries application/problem+json, the type is document-invalid (422), the detail names the missing field, and no ledger file is written for the invalid envelope.
definition_of_done.expected: exit 0 and a closing line `passed 29, failed 0`, with section 5 printing `ok   malformed envelope exits 2 (2)`, `ok   answer is problem details`, `ok   typed as document-invalid (422)`, `ok   names the missing field`, `ok   nothing written for an invalid envelope`.
definition_of_done.breakage: In `examples/end-to-end/run.py`, replace the body of `fail()` - the line that prints `PROBLEM (application/problem+json):` followed by the JSON body - with `print("ERROR: " + str(problem))`, so the same failure is returned as prose. Change nothing else.
definition_of_done.expected_failure: exit 1 and `passed 25, failed 4`: section 5 reports `FAIL not problem details` and `FAIL not typed`, and section 4 reports `FAIL not typed` and `FAIL wrong step`, because the budget refusal stops being machine-readable at the same moment. `ok   names the missing field` still passes, which is the useful part: the words survived and the contract did not, so a caller that string-matched would have seen nothing wrong.
definition_of_done.quote: Typed and machine-readable. Never parsed from prose

open_questions.question: Should a caller ever see causes, or is the delegated chain internal?
open_questions.evidence: Count, across recorded failures, how often the innermost cause changes what a caller does. If it never does, causes is diagnostic material that belongs in the platform-side record keyed by correlation identifier rather than in the body a caller receives.
open_questions.default: Keep causes on the body and tell callers to read it only for reporting, never for branching. Removing a member later is cheaper than adding one after clients exist.
